title: Clinical Mastery: Goldmann Applanation Tonometry (GAT)
summary: Goldmann Applanation Tonometry remains the gold standard for intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement, relying on the Imbert-Fick principle. Precision is paramount in glaucoma screening, surgical planning, and long-term management.

sections.title: Definition & Principle
sections.content: GAT is a contact method that measures the force required to flatten a fixed area (3.06 mm diameter) of the cornea. It is based on the Imbert-Fick Law: P = F / A, where Pressure (P) equals Force (F) applied over Area (A). For the cornea, when A is 3.06 mm, the capillary attraction of the tear film and corneal rigidity negate each other, allowing the force reading to directly approximate IOP in mmHg.

sections.title: Clinical Setup & Procedure
content: Step 1: Instill proparacaine and fluorescein sodium.
Step 2: Align the blue cobalt filter and set the biprism to 0 position.
Step 3: Advance the tonometer head until the biprism touches the apex.
Step 4: View through the slit lamp; align the inner edges of the two semi-circles.
Step 5: Record the reading when the edges are perfectly aligned (10x magnification).

sections.title: Red Flags: Procedural Errors
content: Do not apply excessive pressure (can induce vasovagal response or corneal abrasion).
Avoid contact with patients with active corneal ulcers (infectious transmission risk).
Disinfect biprism with 70% isopropyl alcohol for at least 5 minutes to prevent adenovirus transmission.
Ensure proper alignment (misalignment creates vertical shift of semi-circles).

content.explanation: T-ouch (Gentle contact), H-orizontal (Ensure semi-circles are level), E-dge (Align the inner margins perfectly).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Calibration check: Perform weekly using the standardized weight block (0, 2, and 6 g).
Astigmatism > 3.0D: Align the biprism mark with the patient's minus-cylinder axis.
Always dry the biprism after disinfection to prevent chemical keratitis.
IOP is typically highest in the morning; repeat measurements may be needed for diurnal curves.
Wait 10-15 minutes after topical anesthetic before performing Schirmer's testing.
